title: SDK transactional helpers and permission model for safe rollouts
creator: Lena Kim
description:
Summary: Define and deliver an SDK + API contract that provides transactional helpers for creating, advancing, and aborting model rollouts with strong idempotency guarantees and fine-grained permission scopes. This work enables safe canary rollouts, A/B experiments, shadow traffic flows, and automatic rollback triggers without requiring callers to implement complex retry or reconciliation logic.

Goals:
- API endpoints for atomic rollout operations (create, checkpoint, advance, pause, abort, finalize) with idempotency tokens and explicit intent semantics.
- SDK client helpers that wrap the API to provide opinionated primitives: Transaction object, Checkpoint/Commit semantics, SafeAdvanceWithAudit, ShadowAttach/Detach helpers.
- Permission model scoped to rollout primitives (e.g., rollout.create, rollout.advance.canary, rollout.abort) to limit blast radius.
- Comprehensive server-side audit events exported to Console and Kafka for traceability.
- Backfill acceptance tests and a simple migration guide for existing rollout users.

Non-goals:
- Implementing the low-level routing/fallback logic for every model variant — the runtime teams will handle routing.
- Full client SDKs for every language in this ticket; initial delivery is TypeScript + Python reference implementations.

Proposed API surface (high level):
- POST /v1/rollouts  -> create rollout request, returns rollout_id and initial checkpoint id. Supports idempotency-key header.
- POST /v1/rollouts/{id}/checkpoint -> create a stable checkpoint representing current traffic allocation.
- POST /v1/rollouts/{id}/advance -> advance to next checkpoint (body includes targetCheckpointId, optional safety checks).
- POST /v1/rollouts/{id}/pause -> pause in-flight rollout.
- POST /v1/rollouts/{id}/abort -> abort and rollback to last known good checkpoint.
- POST /v1/rollouts/{id}/shadow -> attach/detach shadow target variants.
Each mutating endpoint must accept: idempotency_key, client_tx_id, and an optional dry_run flag.

SDK primitives (reference):
- RolloutClient.createRollout(params, opts) -> returns RolloutTransaction handle with commit()/checkpoint() and auto-retry on transient failures.
- RolloutTransaction.safeAdvance(nextCheckpoint, {hysteresisMs, minSamples, qualityChecks}) -> waits for minimum metrics or time before advancing; exposes cancellation token.
- RolloutClient.attachShadow(rolloutId, target, samplingRate) -> lightweight helper that wires shadow traffic without impacting decision plane.
- RolloutClient.watch(rolloutId, {metrics, events}) -> returns async iterator stream for lifecycle events (used by console and infra tests).

Idempotency strategy:
- Server-side canonicalization by idempotency_key + client_tx_id + actor. The server will store results of initial operation keyed by these values for a configurable TTL (30 days default).
- Client SDKs will surface retriable vs non-retriable errors and provide built-in exponential backoff and jitter.
- For multi-step flows (create -> checkpoint -> advance), the SDK will expose a transaction object that records the last-observed checkpoint id, allowing resumes after partial failures.

Permission model and authz: 
- New scopes: rollout:create, rollout:modify, rollout:advance, rollout:abort, rollout:shadow, rollout:read.
- RBAC roles map: "Release Engineer" -> {create, modify, advance, pause}; "Platform Operator" -> {abort, shadow, read}.
- SDK will include a helper to request pre-signed temporary tokens for cross-service operations where needed.
- Audit metadata: every mutating call must include actor, origin (SDK version, IP region), and an optional change_reason field for human-readable context.

Observability and rollout safety hooks:
- Emit structured events: rollout.created, checkpoint.created, rollout.advanced, rollout.paused, rollout.aborted, rollout.finalized. Events include checkpoint id, allocations, metrics snapshot.
- Console will surface live diff view of traffic allocation per checkpoint and allow fast rollback to last good checkpoint.
- Auto-rollback: API accepts a list of trigger conditions (latency_p99 > X, error_rate > Y, quality_regression > Z) that the runtime monitors; when triggered, server will transition to abort state and produce an audit event.

Acceptance criteria:
- API spec documented and reviewed by ENG and Security.
- TypeScript + Python SDK helpers implementing transaction primitives with unit tests and integration tests against staging.
- End-to-end test demonstrating a canary rollout with checkpoint, safe advance using hysteresis and a simulated metric regression that triggers auto-rollback.
- RBAC scopes wired into the Console UI and a sample policy mapping.
- Security review completed and audit events flowing to the analytics pipeline.

Rollout plan for this ticket:
1) Design review (this ticket) with ENG, Security, Console owners — target 2026-02-19.
2) API prototype + server skeleton (ENG) — 2 weeks.
3) SDK reference + integration tests (PM + DX) — 1 week.
4) Console wiring for visibility and manual abort controls — 1 week.
5) Security review & staging verification — 3 days.

Risks and mitigations:
- Race conditions across concurrent advance/abort calls: mitigate with server-side serializable intent and optimistic concurrency (checkpoint version).
- Misuse of idempotency tokens causing stale state: SDK will default to generating high-entropy client_tx_id and document best practices.
- Permission gaps causing unauthorized aborts: enforce least-privilege scopes and require two-person approval for aborts on high-impact rollouts.

Open questions:
- TTL for idempotency records — propose 30 days default, configurable per org.
- How to expose simulation/dry-run mode in Console for non-destructive testing.
- Whether shadow attachments should be rate-limited by org-level quotas.
